However, if you, like many others, find command-line tools a bit intimidating, feel more like a designer than a programmer, or simply haven’t had the time to experiment with it yet, this guide is designed for you.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[{\"_key\":\"d135dfe4adff\",\"_type\":\"link\",\"href\":\"https://unity.com/blog/meet-the-unity-cli\"}],\"style\":\"normal\"}],\"blockIndex\":1,\"blockType\":\"mangoRichText\",\"blockKey\":\"mangoRichText-0\",\"container\":\"xs\"}]}],[\"$\",\"div\",\"block-1\",{\"children\":[\"$\",\"$L1c\",\"block-1\",{\"_type\":\"mangoRichText\",\"settings\":null,\"content\":[{\"_key\":\"2eda2482ed59\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"22fb63e19636\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"What is the Unity CLI?\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"h2\"},{\"_key\":\"2c210f178051\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"420955d6bc41\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"One of the Unity's Editor’s greatest strengths is the GUI, which makes it easy to visually manage complex projects. Inspecting a prefab, tweaking material values, running tests, baking lighting, or tracking down console errors are all just a few mouse clicks away in the Editor. This workflow has served users for almost two decades, it has become the bottleneck for repetitive tasks, automation, and AI-driven (agentic) workflows. An AI agent can navigate clicks and visual-only interfaces, but this requires an extra, non-native layer of visual interpretation that slows down the process and adds unneeded overhead, which quickly consumes tokens.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"fb2b4dc88fa3\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"41db76e1d318\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"This is where the new Unity CLI and the experimental Unity Pipeline package come in.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"eabdbb91899d\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"709bf08b63ad\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"The Unity CLI is, as its name suggests, a Command Line Interface for managing Unity. Because it has no graphical user interface, it’s exceptionally well-suited for automation and agentic workflows. It works as a self-contained binary (application) that includes what it needs to run, manage, and interface with Unity. In other words, you can run commands from the terminal that talks straight to Unity, replacing the layer of mouse clicks and entire workflows in the Hub or Editor.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"6d00ead96caf\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"237c0008cf3a\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[\"strong\"],\"text\":\"Note: \"},{\"_key\":\"201245aca781\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"New features and improvements are being added frequently. (\"},{\"_key\":\"653249a68de0\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[\"strong\",\"code\"],\"text\":\"com.unity.pipeline\"},{\"_key\":\"6453abc1f4ab\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\").\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"}],\"blockIndex\":3,\"blockType\":\"mangoRichText\",\"blockKey\":\"mangoRichText-2\",\"container\":\"xs\"}]}]\n1e:[\"$\",\"div\",\"block-3\",{\"children\":[\"$\",\"$L3e\",\"block-3\",{\"_type\":\"mangoMediaBlock\",\"settings\":{\"isHidden\":null,\"theme\":\"light\",\"padding\":null},\"videoType\":\"none\",\"layout\":\"full\",\"mediaType\":\"single\",\"aspectRatio\":\"none\",\"fit\":\"cover\",\"image\":{\"asset\":{\"url\":\"https://cdn.sanity.io/images/fuvbjjlp/production/42de85453be72bd51bd61cc726ee6fedc29f7854-1200x675.png\",\"metadata\":{\"lqip\":\"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABQAAAALCAYAAAB/Ca1DAAAACXBIWXMAAAsSAAALEgHS3X78AAACFUlEQVQokU2TWVIbMRRFewOxsXugB7ekng0YU8YjgYAJYwIpBgMfqWwhgaSyhti7PinJ4OLj1H3D1dWPZNVrTVzHY93zjdpNl2bDwbE90zv2stdz3Xvuutm9n7nOsq99aGDppRSKqqwoi4pEJYhYkqWZmeVZjhQSJRVFUdBut8nS3HiUTCjywiBiYS6wwqhNZ/uc0eSR0fiJ3f49vd1b+sN7xmb2QH94x2B4y2jywHjvicFwZjzaOxw/GLY6ZwRhhSXTT4wOfjO9XHB0seDw/B9HF5o5x5cLTq4WnF5rnfP564Lpl7nZac/h+Vs9Z/DxmVjtY3myTzb6wcb0mWr6i+roJ5vHz3RP/7BztqR79sL2yYupexd/jWqP9lavJIPvuHEPqx6W2J0p7uAb7uDaEIxvEPv3yIMZcn9Ga++OaHKHOpiRHT4a9Uc3OP2rFc2tKbWgwKrZIY5o42XdJelS17Mufr5DvDFAdSYGuTkiKnv4eRc33cZRnRXNVkmtGWCt1V3CUCJVjpApUSQJQ0EQxKZWKifPN2hXHapyC6UKoki9eoTxaTw3oF63sRprrjEkaYk0gYIwiA1RKIhbkjhOSHRwVpEmBa2WDlx63tCBazpQp7pugO9HeF6A6/or9CyOFVKkCJEghCIIWnj6E7zzaeymt3zYtVpj9TPsV3StCfyINM0pCv3AS5IkM5e87d+faTRcE/gfdbVE7kLu66EAAAAASUVORK5CYII=\",\"dimensions\":{\"width\":1200,\"height\":675}}},\"alt\":null,\"aspectRatio\":\"none\",\"fit\":\"cover\",\"crop\":null,\"hotspot\":null},\"images\":null,\"youtubeVideo\":null,\"brandfolderVideo\":{\"inline\":false},\"caption\":null,\"consent\":{\"blockedMessage\":[{\"_key\":\"2f250b735163\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"2f30b996a6c70\",\"_ty Please set your cookie preferences for Targeting Cookies to yes if you wish to view videos from these providers.\"}],\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"}],\"consentButtonLabel\":\"Cookie settings\"},\"blockIndex\":4,\"blockType\":\"mangoMediaBlock\",\"blockKey\":\"mangoMediaBlock-3\",\"container\":\"sm\"}]}]\n1f:[\"$\",\"div\",\"block-4\",{\"children\":[\"$\",\"$L1c\",\"block-4\",{\"_type\":\"mangoRichText\",\"settings\":{\"isHidden\":null,\"theme\":\"light\",\"padding\":null},\"content\":[{\"_key\":\"c4e65e87ebf0\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"954268187411\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"This Unity Pipeline package essentially turns your running Editor into a local HTTP server. Because the Editor stays open in the background, your loaded scenes and asset database remain \\\"warm\\\" in system memory. By keeping everything pre-loaded, you entirely bypass the frustrating startup overhead of booting the engine from a cold state. Your terminal (or an AI agent) can now drive the Editor instantly to run tests, load scenes, or modify GameObjects.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"30caa9e36bbc\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"5a692c771dac\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"e75a048150ce\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"b3c25ff47315\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"The system also handles the notorious domain reload bottleneck. Before the Pipeline package, whenever you or your AI agent made direct changes to a C# script on disk, you had to wait for Unity to rebuild the project and reload the domain. Some actions would even require you to focus or click something in the Editor before it could proceed.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"2d47ffe59004\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"456aafd5cc2c\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"b62fb95a3746\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"d37b49f62f97\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"But the Pipeline package's local server handles that compilation process completely asynchronously. The connection remains stable and active throughout the compile, ensuring your terminal session never drops or times out while the Editor reloads in the background.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"65500adc82ae\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"f29ec5ff89e9\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"e2c9ea877845\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"489b072cd409\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"Things get even faster when you execute code dynamically via the \"},{\"_key\":\"73c6d2c8b1a1\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[\"strong\",\"code\"],\"text\":\"eval\"},{\"_key\":\"310f7107cbd3\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\" command. Here, the Pipeline package in the Editor acts like an instant translator, compiling your C# snippet on the fly and slipping it directly onto Unity's main thread. Because this dynamic execution is entirely self-contained, it completely bypasses the project-wide recompile and domain reload process. You skip the tedious waiting entirely and get your results back in milliseconds.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"77d1be492175\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"464f20d24a27\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"8ffd55d5cb00\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"4cf60002a5d6\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"This means your heavy-duty automation scripts won't crash or lose their connection just because a massive project compile is happening in the background, while your quick terminal commands still fire with near-zero lag. You get stability and speed in the exact same tool.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"e8c6d916919f\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"148ccadec9cb\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"eaa513aa88d8\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"080f86238c53\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"Moving from MCP to the Unity CLI\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"h2\"},{\"_key\":\"2b89b15906b1\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"064051bb8054\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"You might be wondering, “What about the official Unity Model Context Protocol (MCP) server? Why shouldn't I just use or stick with that?”\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"89d653547c71\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"dc0ebd95eb03\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"91c7e5acc3cb\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"1251bb12bbef\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"The short answer is that we’re not dropping the MCP support. However, the Unity CLI and Pipeline package handle all the same use cases as the MCP and more, but do them far better and faster.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"096f853a50d4\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"a7f5e37cb8d7\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"b264cb2e4aa0\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"1d662c5156e3\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"The longer answer comes down to architecture. Traditional MCP setups require an active client harness (like Claude Desktop or Cursor) to act as a translator between your AI agent and Unity. But modern, terminal-native agents like Claude Code are already incredibly good at running standard shell commands directly. By using direct CLI inputs like \"},{\"_key\":\"5b33439bd8d7\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[\"strong\",\"code\"],\"text\":\"unity command\"},{\"_key\":\"a1ac7aa911a3\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\" or \"},{\"_key\":\"9f5cbebcaca0\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[\"strong\",\"code\"],\"text\":\"unity eval\"},{\"_key\":\"fc197cfb61a8\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\", you completely bypass the overhead of configuring and maintaining an MCP server. Your agent gets to talk straight to Unity over a unified, ultra-fast local HTTP server. This means you write cleaner configurations, spend less time debugging connection sockets, and can let your AI operate with pure, native terminal speed.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"dff6fbab3ec3\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"543fb61af5f3\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"67203d61ba28\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"1dc6fc260718\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"Additionally, the \"},{\"_key\":\"cb80019bb8a0\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[\"5abc49661f28\"],\"text\":\"legacy MCP server\"},{\"_key\":\"2e01eca7d740\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\" ran directly inside the Editor process as a C# package. This meant the connection bridge itself was bound to Unity's main thread and memory space. The second you compiled code or triggered a domain reload, Unity flushed its memory, which frequently caused the connection socket to drop, throw null exceptions, or stall the agent mid-loop.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[{\"_key\":\"5abc49661f28\",\"_type\":\"link\",\"href\":\"https://docs.unity.com/en-us/unity-cli/replace-mcp-server-unity-cli\"}],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"6b81b38e5a00\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"7f2ce9ff5594\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"6523cca2eef1\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"77c46ea0119e\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"The current \"},{\"_key\":\"16efc2a2b5cc\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[\"strong\",\"code\"],\"text\":\"com.unity.pipeline\"},{\"_key\":\"a5763975a078\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\" package is also a C# package running inside the Editor, but it exposes an HTTP server and REST API (not a socket bridge), which is why it's more resilient to domain reloads. Because this local server handles commands asynchronously, your terminal connection remains completely stable and active even during heavy compiles and domain reloads.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"1540306698b1\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"8936a3192ad4\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"865d170b5d5e\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"d80302b64667\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"In summary, by moving to the Unity CLI, you completely avoid dropped connections and wasted tokens. Finally, the CLI also offers an MCP mode if you have a specific use case you want to use MCP for.\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"ac4da4b732c8\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"2b74cb1935b7\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"normal\"},{\"_key\":\"0cf40fe86fb8\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"6d88e7bdce40\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"Installing the CLI and Pipeline package\"}],\"file\":null,\"markDefs\":[],\"style\":\"h3\"},{\"_key\":\"a0b6ea1d5ea9\",\"_type\":\"block\",\"children\":[{\"_key\":\"aba809763525\",\"_type\":\"span\",\"marks\":[],\"text\":\"Installing the CLI and Pipeline packages is done automatically with the Unity Hub in the latest versions.
